subject: chemistry

resources.title: Chemistry 2e
resources.notes: Two-semester general chemistry scope; use foundation mapping only for its introductory/review material, not for the entire text.

resources.title: Principles of Chemical Science
resources.notes: Freshman-level independent-study chemistry. Covers atomic/molecular electronic structure, bonding, thermodynamics, equilibrium, redox, transition metals, kinetics and catalysis; high-school review material supports only introductory cells.

resources.title: Principles of Chemical Science
resources.notes: More mathematically demanding introductory chemistry for students with a strong chemistry background; not mapped downward to foundation/beginner.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Chemistry Collection
resources.notes: Discovery collection only; individual courses must be verified before exact-cell ingestion.

resources.title: PubChem
resources.notes: Authoritative chemical information database; database access alone does not establish learner readiness.

resources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.notes: Reference data layer for thermochemical, thermophysical and spectral work; not treated as a stand-alone curriculum.

known_gaps: Dedicated foundation/beginner curricula remain thin for analytical chemistry, biochemistry and materials chemistry.

Graduate and research-level readiness still requires exact advanced courses, current primary literature, laboratory or computational practice, verification and assessment rather than database access alone.
Specialist areas such as spectroscopy, electrochemistry and laboratory methods should only be mapped when their exact taxonomy cells and source evidence are verified.
